events.title: A spilled glass of gin
events.prose: Julian spilled his drink when Maren laughed too loudly at the corner table. He wiped the wet mahogany with a trembling hand, but never met her eyes again.

events.title: The engine part arrived late
events.prose: Caleb waited by the docks for a crate that never came. He sat on the edge of the pier, staring at the oily tide and wondering if the rust had finally won.

events.title: An unspoken debt at breakfast
events.prose: Elias sat in the booth across from Ada, staring at a cold cup of coffee. He opened his mouth to say something about the previous night, but the words died in his throat.

events.title: Missing ledger at the store
events.prose: Ada found the ledger drawer pulled slightly ajar during her morning inventory. Someone had been looking for something specific, leaving only the scent of salt and old paper behind.

memories.text: He sat in the diner booth and watched the steam vanish from his coffee while Ada looked away.
He kept the small, rusted key hidden in the lining of his coat.
He owed Julian Vane three months of back rent for the room above the harbor.
Julian hid the rusted key beneath the loose floorboard of his office.
He watched Ada walk toward the pier through the fogged window of the Mariner Hotel Bar.
He owed Maren Voss three months of silence regarding the shipment from Pier 9.
Maren watched Ada slip a heavy envelope into her coat pocket behind the Blackwood General Store.
She left a chipped ceramic bird on Ada's windowsill as a silent apology for the shouting match at the Rusty Anchor.
Maren practiced her loud, jarring laugh in the mirror until it sounded like genuine joy.
Caleb spent the morning scrubbing grease from his knuckles after a long night at the docks.
He watched Ada walk past the workshop window with a shadow in her eyes that he couldn't repair.
He owed Julian Vane three months of back rent on the small shed behind the harbor.
